question: Do the inferred baryonic origins remain stable if the halo-arrival target may draw from only part of the available baryonic launch capacity instead of forcing every galaxy to route in proportion to its light?

formula.optimization: min sum_ij P_ij |y_j-x_i|^2 + epsilon sum_ij P_ij(log(P_ij)-1)
formula.implementation: A zero-cost unused-capacity sink makes the inequality an exactly balanced augmented transport problem.
formula.interpretation: q_cap is an inverse attribution capacity, not the physical gravity amplitude q and not a fitted cluster parameter.

limits: Capacity relaxation identifies economical origins but does not measure how much gravity any galaxy can reroute.
The posterior halo target remains model-dependent and comes from the same lens observations.
The capacity values are a sensitivity grid, not fitted or promoted constants.
A forward law still must predict destinations from baryons alone on unused raw lens data.
